title: When you land
body:
International arrival is Tokyo (Haneda or Narita, whichever has the better transpacific fare on your dates) — there's no direct US flight to Fukuoka or Sapporo, so a Tokyo connection is unavoidable on the way in. Given a ~13-hour flight lands mid-afternoon to evening, plan to overnight near the Tokyo airport rather than rushing a same-day domestic connection — a short buffer night beats a blown connection after a redeye, and it matches the trip's stated slow pace.

Buy an IC card (Suica/Pasmo) at the airport the moment you land — the chip-shortage sales suspension that hit these in 2023 fully resolved by March 2025, so regular cards, Welcome Suica, and Welcome Suica Mobile are all back in stock. Get an eSIM or pocket wifi active before you leave the arrivals hall (see Phone & data below). The next morning, fly Tokyo → Fukuoka to actually start the trip.

title: Local essentials
body:
Cash matters more than in most countries you've traveled. Card acceptance has broadened at tourist-facing venues, but yatai stalls run roughly 90% cash-only, and plenty of small ramen counters and markets are cash-only too. 7-Eleven ATMs (Seven Bank) are the reliable fallback — they accept Visa, Mastercard, Amex, JCB, Discover and UnionPay 24/7 at ~28,000 machines nationwide, for a per-withdrawal fee on top of whatever your home bank charges. Carry {{fact:local-essentials-1-000}} notes for stalls that can't break a {{fact:local-essentials-10-000}} bill.

Tipping doesn't happen anywhere in Japan — restaurants, taxis, hotels, guides. The one soft exception is an envelope tip for exceptional ryokan staff service, and even that's optional.

Power: Japan runs 100V, Type A plugs (same shape as the US, lower voltage) — most modern phone/laptop chargers auto-handle 100–240V, but check the brick before assuming.

title: Entry & documents
moreLabel: Tax-free shopping — the Nov 1 system change
body:
US passport holders enter visa-free for tourism, up to 90 days — see the Entry card in your Trip kit for the sourced detail. Visit Japan Web (pre-filed immigration/customs QR) is optional, not required — paper landing cards are still accepted planeside. Japan's planned digital pre-arrival system doesn't launch until FY2028, so it doesn't touch this trip.

Tax-free shopping straddles a system change mid-trip. Purchases through Oct 31, 2026 use the current instant-discount system: show your passport at checkout, tax-free price applied on the spot, {{fact:entry-documents-5-000}} (pre-tax) minimum per store per day, keep items sealed until departure. From Nov 1, 2026, Japan switches to a refund-at-departure model: you pay the full tax-inclusive price at checkout, then scan your passport at an airport departure kiosk before check-in so customs can confirm the export electronically, with the refund following afterward (must claim within 90 days — trivial on this trip). Practical read for the gaming/anime shopping days: do any big purchases in Fukuoka and Hokkaido by Oct 31 for the simpler system; anything bought in Sendai in November needs the full sticker price at checkout and extra time at the Tokyo departure airport for the kiosk step.

title: Phone & data
body: For ~26 days of data, an eSIM is the cheapest, most flexible option — and matters more than it sounds for two people who might split up on a shopping or arcade afternoon, since a single shared pocket wifi puck doesn't help if you're on opposite sides of a mall. Ubigi's 20GB/30-day plan runs {{fact:phone-data-19}} unlimited/30-day {{fact:phone-data-65}} — activation is clean, the plan starts the moment you validate it in-app. Airalo's comparable plans run {{fact:phone-data-18}}–25 for 10–20GB. ⚠ "Unlimited" plans on every major eSIM provider (Ubigi, Airalo, Holafly) have a repeated, unresolved user complaint about throttling past a daily threshold — if you're shooting a lot of photo/video and navigating heavily, budget for the higher tier or carry a data top-up option as backup rather than assuming true-unlimited speed. Buy an eSIM before you land (installs over home wifi, activates on arrival).

title: Booking checklist
body: The trip needs three separate domestic flights (Tokyo→Fukuoka, Fukuoka→Sapporo, Sapporo→Sendai) plus the transpacific in/out of Tokyo — book these early since they anchor everything else. The Zao Onsen ryokan (the belated-birthday night) is worth locking in as soon as dates are firm — it's a small, historic property, not a big chain with endless rooms.
checklist: Transpacific flights — into and out of Tokyo (HND/NRT)
Domestic flights: Tokyo → Fukuoka, Fukuoka → Sapporo, Sapporo → Sendai
Confirm exact trip start (Oct 15 or Oct 22) before booking anything — this ripples into every date below
Miyamaso Takamiya ryokan, Zao Onsen — book directly (reserve.489ban.net) once dates are firm
Accommodation — Fukuoka (Tenjin/Hakata area), Sapporo (Susukino/Odori area), Sendai (near the station)
eSIM (Ubigi/Airalo) — buy before departure, install over home wifi
JR Kyushu rail pass (Northern, 5-day) and/or JR East–South Hokkaido Rail Pass, if the point-to-point fare comparison favors them — check closer to travel
Pokémon GO Wild Area Sendai tickets — sales not yet open as of this check; watch pokemongo.com and buy immediately once they open, past events have sold out
Any timed museum/attraction tickets that come up once dates are locked
